_comment: A fieldOverride REPLACES Firestore's automatic indexing for that field — it
does not add to it. These two were written to enable the collection-group
queries the leaderboard and reports need, and in doing so they silently
removed the ordinary single-collection index every other query relies on.
The effect was invisible until something read one user's own subcollection in
order: GET /admin/employees/:id and GET /progress/:userId both do
orderBy('submittedAt','desc') on one user's quizAttempts, and both were
failing with FAILED_PRECONDITION and returning 500. The admin employee page
showed '0 Lessons Done' and 'No quiz attempts yet' for an account with 43
attempts and 23 completed lessons, because the whole response errored rather
than any one field being wrong.
So both scopes are declared explicitly. COLLECTION is what a per-user query
needs; COLLECTION_GROUP is what the cross-user aggregates need.
